k: I was just — admiring. Professionally.
src: 'I was just — admiring. Professionally.'

k: Twelve in the spring!
src: 'Twelve in the spring!'

k: Eleven, then.
src: 'Eleven, then.'

k: Eleven and a _HALF_.
src: 'Eleven and a _HALF_.'

k: You're the only one of them without a light on you. I can feel it. Like a cold spot in a warm bath.
src: 'You\'re the only one of them without a light on you. I can feel it. Like a cold spot in a warm bath.'

k: Yeah, well. Choir says sixteen. Rules is rules. Not that I care. Crests are for people with houses.
src: 'Yeah, well. Choir says sixteen. Rules is rules. Not that I care. Crests are for people with houses.'

k: _(quietly)_ Is that what they told you?
src: '_(quietly)_ Is that what they told you?'

k: ...Nobody had to tell me.
src: '...Nobody had to tell me.'

k: The world's getting darker, little cat. I can't see much. But I can see that.
src: 'The world\'s getting darker, little cat. I can\'t see much. But I can see that.'

k: I'd like you to have something to hold on to.
src: 'I\'d like you to have something to hold on to.'

k: Keeper — you can't. Kindling a child is forbidden. There are laws—
src: 'Keeper — you can\'t. Kindling a child is forbidden. There are laws—'

k: Five years in an Aurenne cell, I believe. Are you going to tell on me, Mender?
src: 'Five years in an Aurenne cell, I believe. Are you going to tell on me, Mender?'

k: ...I'm going to write it down somewhere and not tell anyone where.
src: '...I\'m going to write it down somewhere and not tell anyone where.'

k: Is it... safe? For him?
src: 'Is it... safe? For him?'

k: Nothing worth doing is safe, squire. You of all people know that.
src: 'Nothing worth doing is safe, squire. You of all people know that.'

k: Yes, ma'am.
src: 'Yes, ma\'am.'

k: Well, Pipkin Tallow? Will you step into my light?
src: 'Well, Pipkin Tallow? Will you step into my light?'

k: How do you know my— nobody calls me—
src: 'How do you know my— nobody calls me—'

k: ...Yeah. Yeah, okay. Yes.
src: '...Yeah. Yeah, okay. Yes.'

k: Pip stands in the Lantern's light. His fists are clenched. His chin is up. He looks very small.
src: 'Pip stands in the Lantern\'s light. His fists are clenched. His chin is up. He looks very small.'

k: The light goes all the way through him, warm as fresh bread — and for the first time anyone can remember, Pip forgets to look for the exits.
src: 'The light goes all the way through him, warm as fresh bread — and for the first time anyone can remember, Pip forgets to look for the exits.'

k: ROGUE?! The light called me a _THIEF?!_
src: 'ROGUE?! The light called me a _THIEF?!_'

k: ...I mean. Fair.
src: '...I mean. Fair.'

k: Pip's Crest awakens — *Rogue*! His Crest Arts can now be used in battle.
src: 'Pip\'s Crest awakens — *Rogue*! His Crest Arts can now be used in battle.'

k: Wren. _Wren!_ I got one! I got a Crest! Nobody from the gutters ever— not before sixteen, not _ever_, some of 'em—
src: 'Wren. _Wren!_ I got one! I got a Crest! Nobody from the gutters ever— not before sixteen, not _ever_, some of \'em—'

k: Make way! Rogue Pipkin Tallow, first of his name!
src: 'Make way! Rogue Pipkin Tallow, first of his name!'

k: Put me DOWN, you big— okay, don't put me down yet.
src: 'Put me DOWN, you big— okay, don\'t put me down yet.'

k: Welcome to the trade, kid. Rule one: never tell anyone your real age.
src: 'Welcome to the trade, kid. Rule one: never tell anyone your real age.'

k: Way ahead of you.
src: 'Way ahead of you.'

k: Pip has a light now. It is small. It is very loud.
src: 'Pip has a light now. It is small. It is very loud.'

k: Tamsin laughs — a real laugh, surprised out of her.
src: 'Tamsin laughs — a real laugh, surprised out of her.'

k: They usually are, the small ones.
src: 'They usually are, the small ones.'

k: Go on, all of you. The caravans for the Greyspine leave from the north yard. Ask for Oyelaran, and tell him I said he owes me.
src: 'Go on, all of you. The caravans for the Greyspine leave from the north yard. Ask for Oyelaran, and tell him I said he owes me.'

k: And Wren Halloway — you walk like someone leaving. Make sure you know what you're walking toward.
src: 'And Wren Halloway — you walk like someone leaving. Make sure you know what you\'re walking toward.'

k: Tip — Pip can fight now! Bring him into the active party from the menu's *Formation* screen.
src: 'Tip — Pip can fight now! Bring him into the active party from the menu\'s *Formation* screen.'

k: Keeper Tamsin listened to the fork and said it sings a note she almost knows. She sent us to Brother Halvard at Frosthollow. Then she Kindled Pip. ILLEGALLY. He's a Rogue. He hasn't stopped grinning, and neither has Bram.
src: 'Keeper Tamsin listened to the fork and said it sings a note she almost knows. She sent us to Brother Halvard at Frosthollow. Then she Kindled Pip. ILLEGALLY. He\'s a Rogue. He hasn\'t stopped grinning, and neither has Bram.'

k: Tolle brought the little ones down the mountain. They sing on my steps every morning.
src: 'Tolle brought the little ones down the mountain. They sing on my steps every morning.'

k: Badly. Loudly. Halvard would be delighted.
src: 'Badly. Loudly. Halvard would be delighted.'

k: ...I heard his bell, you know. From here. The whole desert heard it.
src: '...I heard his bell, you know. From here. The whole desert heard it.'

k: Cassian, as a boy? He used to sit right where you're standing and ask me why the sun needed help to come back.
src: 'Cassian, as a boy? He used to sit right where you\'re standing and ask me why the sun needed help to come back.'

k: I told him it didn't need help. It just liked being asked.
src: 'I told him it didn\'t need help. It just liked being asked.'

k: Your friend with the drifting step. Keep her close, Wren.
src: 'Your friend with the drifting step. Keep her close, Wren.'

k: Something is listening for her. I can hear it listening.
src: 'Something is listening for her. I can hear it listening.'

k: The lamp has been humming at dawn this season. A little lower each morning, like a song deciding something.
src: 'The lamp has been humming at dawn this season. A little lower each morning, like a song deciding something.'

k: Go to Halvard. Ask him what it's deciding.
src: 'Go to Halvard. Ask him what it\'s deciding.'

k: Ask him who the Halcyon's named after, little Keeper. Watch him lie.
src: 'Ask him who the Halcyon\'s named after, little Keeper. Watch him lie.'

k: He's a terrible liar. It's the only honest thing about him.
src: 'He\'s a terrible liar. It\'s the only honest thing about him.'

k: You smell like a sky-pirate I know. Tell Corvin Ashe I can smell him from here.
src: 'You smell like a sky-pirate I know. Tell Corvin Ashe I can smell him from here.'

k: Well, well. Corvin Ashe. Alive. My, my.
src: 'Well, well. Corvin Ashe. Alive. My, my.'

k: Ines! You look radiant. Have you done something with your— knives?
src: 'Ines! You look radiant. Have you done something with your— knives?'

k: Six hundred gold, Corvin. Plus the dignity you cost me when you left through the privy window.
src: 'Six hundred gold, Corvin. Plus the dignity you cost me when you left through the privy window.'

k: ...It was a very dignified privy.
src: '...It was a very dignified privy.'

k: Your captain bet me his lucky coin and lost it. Then he bet the coin I'd won off him and lost it again — on credit. Six hundred.
src: 'Your captain bet me his lucky coin and lost it. Then he bet the coin I\'d won off him and lost it again — on credit. Six hundred.'

k: Corvin's Debts
src: 'Corvin\'s Debts'

k: Velvet Ines, in the Cool Well inn, wants the 600 gold Corvin owes her.
src: 'Velvet Ines, in the Cool Well inn, wants the 600 gold Corvin owes her.'

k: Pay 600 gold
src: 'Pay 600 gold'

k: I'll be here. I'm always here. That's what makes me so frightening.
src: 'I\'ll be here. I\'m always here. That\'s what makes me so frightening.'

k: Sweet of you. Come back when the sweetness has some gold in it.
src: 'Sweet of you. Come back when the sweetness has some gold in it.'

k: A Keeper's girl paying a pirate's debts. The world really is ending.
src: 'A Keeper\'s girl paying a pirate\'s debts. The world really is ending.'

k: Here. It was his. He'll tell you it's lucky. It isn't. It's just always been in his pocket while he was being stubborn.
src: 'Here. It was his. He\'ll tell you it\'s lucky. It isn\'t. It\'s just always been in his pocket while he was being stubborn.'

k: That's my lucky coin.
src: 'That\'s my lucky coin.'

k: It doesn't seem very lucky.
src: 'It doesn\'t seem very lucky.'

k: It's still here, isn't it? So am I. That's the luck.
src: 'It\'s still here, isn\'t it? So am I. That\'s the luck.'

k: Ask him who the Halcyon's named after, little Keeper.
src: 'Ask him who the Halcyon\'s named after, little Keeper.'

k: ...It's a bird. A kingfisher. Very calm. Very— it's a _bird_, Ines.
src: '...It\'s a bird. A kingfisher. Very calm. Very— it\'s a _bird_, Ines.'

k: He sleeps eleven hours a night now. I let him.
src: 'He sleeps eleven hours a night now. I let him.'

k: For nine days I didn't sleep at all. Now we're taking turns being grateful.
src: 'For nine days I didn\'t sleep at all. Now we\'re taking turns being grateful.'

k: The upper gallery of the Glass Caverns. That's where the Kessel caravan went in. Please.
src: 'The upper gallery of the Glass Caverns. That\'s where the Kessel caravan went in. Please.'

k: You've met Nim, haven't you? Everyone meets Nim. She sits at the gate with her lunch.
src: 'You\'ve met Nim, haven\'t you? Everyone meets Nim. She sits at the gate with her lunch.'

k: Her father — my Jorah — went with the Kessel caravan through the Glass Caverns' upper gallery. The short way to the eastern wells. Nine days ago.
src: 'Her father — my Jorah — went with the Kessel caravan through the Glass Caverns\' upper gallery. The short way to the eastern wells. Nine days ago.'

k: The Kessel caravan never came out. Oyelaran says the Queen took it. Everyone says the Queen took it.
src: 'The Kessel caravan never came out. Oyelaran says the Queen took it. Everyone says the Queen took it.'

k: I don't believe it. I won't. Not until somebody has looked.
src: 'I don\'t believe it. I won\'t. Not until somebody has looked.'

k: We'll look.
src: 'We\'ll look.'

k: The Fastest Scout
src: 'The Fastest Scout'

k: Asha's husband Jorah went into the Glass Caverns with the Kessel caravan nine days ago and never came out. Search the caverns beyond Saltglass's east gate.
src: 'Asha\'s husband Jorah went into the Glass Caverns with the Kessel caravan nine days ago and never came out. Search the caverns beyond Saltglass\'s east gate.'

k: Papa came home! He came home and he was SO DIRTY!
src: 'Papa came home! He came home and he was SO DIRTY!'

k: And she made me take a bath before she'd hug me. My own daughter.
src: 'And she made me take a bath before she\'d hug me. My own daughter.'

k: We owe you everything. We don't have everything. We have these.
src: 'We owe you everything. We don\'t have everything. We have these.'

k: His running boots. Fastest scout on the salt road. He says he's finished running.
src: 'His running boots. Fastest scout on the salt road. He says he\'s finished running.'

k: Nine days in a glass box teaches you where you want to be standing.
src: 'Nine days in a glass box teaches you where you want to be standing.'

k: You're the boy with the Crest! The little one!
src: 'You\'re the boy with the Crest! The little one!'

k: I'm not little.
src: 'I\'m not little.'

k: You're littler than Papa.
src: 'You\'re littler than Papa.'

k: ...Everyone's littler than somebody.
src: '...Everyone\'s littler than somebody.'

k: Jorah is home. Nim made him take a bath before she'd hug him. Grandmother Zeyneb took a chime down.
src: 'Jorah is home. Nim made him take a bath before she\'d hug him. Grandmother Zeyneb took a chime down.'
